newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo cen.bank vows to keep its policy unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Yugo cen.bank vows to keep its policy unchanged.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank on Friday vowed to keep its tight monetary policy unchanged until the end of 1996 despite some positive indicators, a central bank official said on Friday.
"The central bank has no reasons to change anything in its current policy," the central bank vice-governor Ratko Banovic told Reuters.
"There will be no relaxation in the central bank monetary policy, and we will not be mislead by any temporarily encouraging data that could provoke some easing," Banovic said.
The basic strategy remains, and if some evidence of growing instability occurs, the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) would have to tighten its policy further, he added.
Banovic described the third quarter of this year as unusually stable.
"We have not witnessed such stability for several years. Normally those three summer months would bring the first toublesome signs that explode during the last quarter of the year," he said.
The NBY's tight monetary policy also closely matches the demands of the International Monetary Fund for expected normalisation of relations.

"We have the necessary degree of restrictiveness and with Yugoslavia rejoining international financial institutions, we look for an increased credit activity. We would begin to receive foreign credits, and hard currency inflow would take the pressure off the demand for dinars," Banovic said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
